facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a new pigmented lesion on his left second toenail
The lesion first appeared 12 months before presentation and was progressively growing
The lesion was asymptomatic
He was otherwise well and denied any fevers or weight loss
dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail of the left second digit with corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band
The pigment was the same width throughout the band and extended to the proximal nail fold
No other nail or skin lesions were found at the time of examination
Bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix with invaginations of the epithelium
No melanocytic lesions observed
Immunostaining negative for S100 and CD34
Intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis present
Villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia

concepts.why: The presence of bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix and villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia supports the diagnosis of Onychomatricoma.

The dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail with corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band suggests melanocytic activation, but the absence of melanocytic lesions on histopathology makes this a less likely diagnosis.
The presence of nail thickening over the pigmented band supports the diagnosis of nail plate thickening, but this is likely a secondary finding related to the primary diagnosis of Onychomatricoma.

The presence of villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate and the absence of melanocytic lesions, as indicated by negative immunostaining for S100 and CD34, along with intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis, are findings that can be associated with onychopapilloma.
